payload.text: Thirty-nine. Same as before. You keep going up, I keep saying the same number.

Ay, cariño, qué cosas dices, me alegras el domingo. Mira — veinticinco P, and I wrap it nice. And a consejo from an old woman: keep your repetidas, hijo. What is nothing to you is gold to the boy who needs it. Now, go eat something, prometido.

¡Cuarenta y seis! Nando, hold the case, my hands are shaking. Listen, amigo — fifty-three P. That is the last word from both mouths, no more dancing, no more goats. Say yes and we shake. Say no and we close the case, walk to the dogs next table. ¿Cincuenta y tres?

Thirty-nine. You can offer the moon, chaval. Number doesn't move.
Diecisiete primas, caballero. Es mi última palabra, se lo digo con toda claridad: si no la acepta, cierro el álbum y damos la tarde por terminada. Ni una prima más. Usted dirá.

"¡Amigo! Perfect timing, we were just packing up—" "—but for you, Paco opens the case again. Look! Casa de las Flores, mint, barely breathed on. Our abuela cried when we found it." "She cried a lot, honestly." Seventy-three pesos and it walks home with you. ¿Sí?
You move, I move. 40 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 64 P.
Buenas. You find me at my desk, as always. I have the San Francisco el Grande. My terms: one hundred thirteen. I am in no hurry, señor.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, have you eaten? Look, this one, the Puesto del Rastro — twelve, for you. A little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Forty years I tell children this.

Ay, mis nietos, bien, gracias a Dios — el mayor ya tiene hijos, imagínate. Cuarenta años aquí, cariño, y todavía me da alegría. Mira, te lo dejo en veinticinco P, y te lo envuelvo bonito. Y luego vas a comer algo, prometido, hijo.
Forty-one. Last one. You say no, I pack up and we both go home.

"¡Otro rato! Amigo, otro rato we're in Sevilla—" "—with the case closed." Listen, 59 P for the Casa de las Flores. That's the last word, Paco's and mine both. Say no and we fold the suitcase, shake your hand, and walk. No hard feelings, never any. ¿Qué dices?
Doscientos sesenta? No, señor. My terms stand: one hundred thirteen for the San Francisco el Grande. The desk does not move. Take your time deciding.

Ay, hijo, qué bonito hablas. Mira — veinticuatro P, y es mi última palabra, de verdad. Si no, guardo la cartita en la caja y seguimos charlando otro domingo, sin enfados. Veinticuatro, envuelta bonita. Y después vas a comer algo, prometido, cariño.

Ay, buenos días, hijo! Have you eaten? Come, look — this one, the Puesto del Rastro, very pretty card. For you, twelve. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

"¡Amigo, qué pena!" "Qué pena de verdad." Forty-three won't buy this one today, not from Paco, not from Nando. So — hand on heart, no hard feelings, none ever. The case closes, we go to Sevilla, you keep your pesos. Come find us another time, ¿eh? ¡Suerte, campeón!
Good evening. Vermut del Domingo, 16 P. I trust that suits you.
Buenas. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Thirty-nine primas. That is the number.
Doscientos cuarenta y ocho changes nothing. One hundred thirteen for the San Francisco el Grande. That is the term, señor. Decide when you wish.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one is Las Vistillas, very pretty card, I give it to you for 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, mucho gusto. You have the face of a collector, yes? Then look fast, because this one goes quick: Casa de las Flores, beautiful thing, corners like glass. Seventy-three P and the suitcase closes. We leave before lunch, eh?

Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 67 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Thirty-nine. Same as before. You are moving down, I am not. Monumento a Alfonso XII, thirty-nine primas.
Buenas tardes, caballero. The Monumento a Alfonso XII — El Retiro, my beloved Retiro. A fine piece, though hardly scarce. I offer sixty-one primas, and I assure you, that is an honest figure.

Ay, cariño, four! You make me laugh like my nieto. Look — ten, and I even throw in my good advice for free. Eat something after, you look thin. And El Chato, next stall, opens at half past nine tonight — he likes honest traders like you.
Querido mío, the Embassy does lovely pastries, but it does not set my prices. Vermut del Domingo, sixteen. That is my figure, and it does not wander.

Ay, qué alegría, hijo, qué bonito verte otra vez. Diez es poquito, mi vida, esa carta tiene su cariño. Mira, te la dejo en 26 P, porque empiezas y me caes bien. ¿Y has comido algo? Luego me traes tus repetidas y las cambiamos, ¿eh?
El Instituto. Thirty-three. You want it or you want to look?
Buenas tardes. Qué gusto. I see you carry the Tienda de Discos — a charming little card, and I have a gap in one album. I offer sixteen pesetas for it. Fair, and paid at once.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment — have you eaten? Look, this one, Puesto del Rastro, very pretty, twelve P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates, eh?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — the Kiosco de Prensa card, very pretty, I keep it in the tin since Sunday. For you, twelve P. My grandson started his album with that one, forty years ago almost.

¡Ay, Chamberí, Chamberí! Paco, close the case— no, wait. Listen, amigo: sixty-three P, and I swear on my mother's paella, this is the last one left in all Madrid. Nobody has another. We looked. Nando cried a little. Sixty-three and it's yours, hombre.

Ay, cariño, doce... eso es para un bocadillo, no para Las Vistillas. Mira, te la dejo en 24 P, que ya bajo otra vez por ti. Y si hoy no llega, vuelves el domingo con tus repetidas y hablamos, que aquí siempre estoy. ¿Comiste algo, hijo?
Forty-one primas now. You keep walking down, I keep walking up. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Forty-one.

Caballero, we are not so far apart in courtesy, but very far in numbers. I know this print run intimately. Sixty-three primas — a small step, and my final courtesy toward El Retiro. Shall we conclude?

¡Cuarenta y cinco! Nando, cover your ears, hombre. Listen: sixty P, Casa de las Flores, corners like glass, and we throw in the story for free. A señora in Chamberí offered more yesterday — we said no, we liked your face. Sesenta, amigo, and the case closes.

¡Amigo! Paco here, Nando there — qué gusto, a man who knows his Lazarillo! Then you know quality. Museo Sorolla, yours for 73 primas. And listen, the team next door is sniffing at it already, but we like your face better. Decide quick, hermano, before they come back.
Doscientos cuarenta y cuatro, no. I will say ciento catorce for the San Francisco el Grande, and not one peseta beyond. The desk waits, señor.

Oh, you're killing us. 58 P.
Buenas. La Chulapa, 13 primas. Esa es la carta que te interesa.

¡Dos primas! Nando, trae la silla, que me caigo. Hermano, con cariño se paga el pan, no el Sorolla. Mira: bajamos a 63 primas, y eso porque tu barrio es el nuestro. Los de al lado vuelven en nada con el dinero en la mano. ¿Cerramos ya, amigo?

Ay, mi vida, qué cosas más bonitas dices. Mira, Las Vistillas te la dejo en 24 P, igual que antes, que ya bajé por ti. Y el regalito sí: te busco una repetida mía para tu página, de abuela a hijo. Pero dime, ¿comiste algo hoy?

Galdiano collected with discipline, señor, not with sentiment. Vermut del Domingo, sixteen primas. The figure has not moved, and it will not. Shall we close it, or shall we admire each other a while longer?
Oh, oh... 11 P, and only because you have a kind face.
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
Let us be civilised: 16 P.
Forty-five. You come down two, I go up two. That is how this works. Monumento a Alfonso XII, forty-five primas.

¡Tres primas! Nando, apunta eso, que nos reímos luego en el taxi. Mira, hermano: 57 primas, el Sorolla es tuyo, y te juro que es cariño puro. Pero corre, que la poli... digo, el taxi nos espera con el motor en marcha. ¿Sí o sí, amigo?
Buenas tardes. You look like someone who takes collecting seriously, so I shall be direct: a gold pack, sealed and pristine, for 504 pesetas. I do not offer these to just anyone.
You again. Silver pack, 188. Good cards in there — better than what Abuela's been handing out. Take it or keep walking.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one here, the Neighbourhood pack — thirty P. Good cards inside for someone starting out. My little Mateo began with one just like it, and now look at him, he beats his father.

¡Cincuenta y cuatro! Amigo, you squeeze like my mother squeezes oranges. Fine — cincuenta y cinco P, Casa de las Flores, the same card, same corners, same story. And this is the last word, hombre. Fifty-five or Nando shuts the suitcase and we walk to the train. ¿Trato?
No. 188 P, and I'm being generous.

A little, you say — yet you have barely moved, caballero. I shall be the generous one: sixty-five primas. That is my affection for El Retiro speaking, not my arithmetic. Shall we shake hands and be done?

Ay, un chotis! You dance it on one tile, cariño, like a real madrileño. My Paco danced it so, barely moving his feet. Seventeen is little, hijo... twenty-six for the Neighbourhood pack, sí? And tonight El Chato opens at half past nine — he likes straight traders like you.

¡La nieta! Nando, el corazón, que se me parte. Mira, hermano: por esa niña, 52 primas y me olvido del margen. Se lo cuentas de mayor, el día que su abuelo regateó con Los Pícaros y ganó. Pero ya, que arranca el taxi. ¿Trato?

¡Ay, mis nietos, bien, gracias, cariño! El mayor vende tebeos, ¡imagínate!

Mira, hijo: 23 P por Las Vistillas, y esta es mi última palabra. Si no, nos damos un abrazo y la guardo para otro domingo, sin enfado ninguno.

¿Y comiste algo ya?
You moved one. So do I. 187. Those other teams? Never seen them at my stall.
Buenas. You come at a quiet hour; that suits me. San Francisco el Grande — the dome card. My terms: one hundred thirteen P. I do not haggle quickly.
Forty-nine. Two from you, two from me. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Forty-nine primas.
Seventeen primas, señor. That is my last word — refuse it and I close the album and we part as friends. One more thing: ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa. Only one printed, they say.

Ay, hijo, eighteen... you make me laugh like my Paco did. Twenty-five, and I will not move from there, con cariño. Look, a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates, always. ¿Has comido algo hoy? Take your time, cariño.
13. No me he movido, y tú tampoco de verdad. La Chulapa, 13 primas. Tómala o vete al vermut.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? No? Later, later. Look here — this one, Puesto del Rastro, very pretty card, my favourite. For you, twelve pesetas. My grandson started his album with this very one, forty years ago, imagine.
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Buenas. Museo Sorolla, treinta y nueve primas. El vermut lo pagas tú.

Caballero, your steps are measured in centimetres while mine are in metres. Sixty-eight primas. I say it with affection for El Retiro, but my patience, like good wine, should not be left open too long.

Buenas tardes. How pleasant to see a serious face at my table. The Museo Sorolla — a charming little card, and one my album still lacks. I offer you forty-seven pesetas for it. Fair, and I do not haggle foolishly.
Fifty-one. That is my last word. Two for two, same as always. Refuse and I walk, and the card stays here. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Fifty-one primas.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
Let us be civilised: 17 P.
Doscientos sesenta, no. I named my terms already: ciento trece P for the dome card. That is what I pay. Take your time deciding.
Querido mío, ciento cuarenta y tres is a fantasy, not a price. I know every print run of that little card. Forty-nine pesetas — a courtesy, not a haggle. Shall we close it elegantly?
Sixty-nine primas, caballero. That is my last word — I will not say another number today. Accept it, or we part politely and this card stays in your pocket, not in my album.
Amigo! Andén 0, 187 P, a gift, a real gift!

Doscientos cuarenta y ocho changes nothing. Ciento trece P stands for the dome card. The number will not move while you shave it. Decide when you wish.
